cardinality_boundary_analysis.boundary_cases_checked: For n=1 or n=2 the strict Appendix-E interior claims are not invoked; the generic LP and Appendix-C statements require only the displayed nonempty domain.
cardinality_boundary_analysis.lean_boundary_evidence: Basic.lean:8-19 fixes User=Fin m and Item=Fin n; PaperInterface.lean carries 2 < n precisely on the Appendix-E statements that use a center/right-half distinction.
cardinality_boundary_analysis.lean_cardinality_domain: Items are Fin n.  The corresponding Appendix E rows carry the literal premise 2 < n; rows without it use only nonemptiness through NeZero n.
cardinality_boundary_analysis.source_cardinality_domain: The source indexes a finite item set by n; Appendix E explicitly assumes n > 2 where an interior/center comparison is used.
cardinality_boundary_analysis.strictness_witness_or_reason: The strict order/center witnesses are supplied only under 2 < n, which yields three finite indices.  No unproved strictness is claimed at smaller n.

carrier_and_domain.lean_bridge: The finite-index definitions and the theorem premises are checked together: nonempty domains support finite minima, while Appendix-E strict/center claims retain the literal 2 < n boundary.
carrier_and_domain.lean_evidence: Basic.lean:8-19 fixes the two finite carriers and the policy action space; the refreshed PaperInterface source elaboration checks the same finite domains in every selected row.
carrier_and_domain.semantic_comparison: The source has m users and n items with finite indexed sums.  Lean uses Fin m and Fin n, with nonemptiness or the explicit n>2 premise exactly where the source's minima or interior pivot arguments require it; it does not replace the finite carrier by an arbitrary type.

conditioning_and_calibration_semantics.lean_evidence: The expanded row contains finite arithmetic and policy PMFs but no conditional-event operator.
conditioning_and_calibration_semantics.semantic_comparison: The selected source result is a deterministic finite LP statement and has no conditioning or calibration operation.

expanded_binders_and_domain.lean_evidence: PaperInterface.lean is freshly elaborated in the current source-record audit; its expanded theorem type is the reviewed binder/result surface and its proof is checked against the local finite-policy definitions.
expanded_binders_and_domain.semantic_comparison: The source statement and expanded Lean row quantify the same finite user/item indices, real parameters, policy variables, and displayed sign/order/LP antecedents.  No result quantifier or endpoint is supplied by a name-only route.

expectation_definedness.lean_evidence: The expanded theorem row has only finite real arithmetic and no expectation operator.
expectation_definedness.semantic_comparison: No expectation/integral occurs in this selected deterministic algebraic result.

extended_rate_codomain.lean_bridge: The checked real-valued formulas retain the stated finite parameter domains and do not claim an infinite-rate extension.
extended_rate_codomain.lean_evidence: The expanded theorem binders use real alpha, beta, epsilon, utility values, and LP levels; no extended-rate codomain or infinity constructor occurs.
extended_rate_codomain.semantic_comparison: All source and Lean parameters here are ordinary finite real utility/tradeoff coefficients.  No rate takes an extended-real/infinite value, so no finite-versus-WithTop convention is hidden.

distribution_parameterization_analysis.family_coupling_evidence: The checked source and expanded Lean surfaces contain no shared base law, latent source, or parameter-indexed sampling construction.
distribution_parameterization_analysis.family_coupling_scope: There is no cross-parameter family: no pair of parameter-indexed random laws is compared, only deterministic policies and finite utility vectors.

distribution_parameterization_analysis.source_scale_or_variance: No source probability-law scale, variance, rate, or precision convention is used in these static LP results.
